Execution: `cd /tmp; (cd /; pwd); pwd` -> "/" then "/tmp"; permissions.sh prints "working directory: /tmp/demo" then "working directory: /" around `cd /`.

Lab box help: whoami "Print the user name associated with the current effective user ID."; mkdir "-p, --parents"; rm "-r, -R, --recursive", "-f, --force". permissions.sh output: printf > app.conf then `cat app.conf` -> "port=8080"; $(whoami) inserted into the echo line ("... running as: root").

Execution: `ls /nope 2>&1 >/dev/null | cat` shows the error on stdout; `false || echo ran` -> "ran", `true || echo notran` prints nothing. permissions.sh: "cat: app.conf: No such file or directory" then "the same relative path now finds nothing".

issues.quote: Start the example system with `scripts/up.sh` — it starts a small Linux machine inside your computer — then run `scripts/computer/permissions.sh` from the same terminal.
issues.text: After this lesson I know `scripts/up.sh` is a relative path, and section 5 warned that the `--project` command runs only from the top folder. Try it does not say where to stand, so the lesson's own point makes me unsure.
issues.fix: Add 'from the top folder of the example system' after 'Start the example system with `scripts/up.sh`'.

issues.quote: So a file can exist, be named correctly, and still refuse to open — a different failure from absence.
issues.text: The diagram asks 'Anything there?' before 'Allowed for this user?', but the prose never says in words that the permission check only happens once something is found at the path. I inferred it from the arrows; q1 depends on that order.
issues.fix: Add one clause: 'the operating system first looks whether anything sits at the finished path, and only then checks whether this user may open it'.

issues.quote: The operating system sees the name does not start at the top of the file tree
issues.text: The lesson never describes this as a separate step the operating system takes; it only defines a relative path as one that does not start at the top. I placed d before a by logic, not from the text, so the item tests reasoning about steps the lesson did not narrate.
issues.fix: Either add to section 4's first paragraph 'seeing that it does not start with `/`, the operating system finishes it with the working directory', or drop option d and order four steps.

issues.quote: It prints that folder, then the folder the program file sits in, then that first folder with `app.conf` added, then `not found:` with that same path.
issues.text: The opening paragraph of section 5 packs the command, what `--` means, the four printed lines, why `--project` is relative, what `.` means, a second command and `RelativePath`. 'that folder' / 'that first folder' / 'that same path' made me re-read it twice.
issues.fix: Replace 'It prints that folder' with 'It prints the working directory', and 'that first folder with `app.conf` added' with 'the working directory with `app.conf` added'.
